correctness.rationale: The cyclic model has 28 vertices with degree three. The frozen Fano verifier checks an explicit bijection to the nonline triples of the Fano plane, preserving the edge sets, and the standard Coxeter definition is the Kneser graph K(7,3) with those seven line vertices deleted. In a proper coloring with at most three colors, each neighborhood has at most two colors; at degree three the only odd multiplicity pattern under this cap is one color three times. Colors must then agree along every even walk. Connectedness and a seven-cycle give an even walk between any two vertices, contradicting properness. For four colors the only allowable neighbor patterns are three equal or three distinct, with no neighbor of the center's color. An independent fixed-vertex-order exhaustive search fixed c₀=0 and tried all four colors at each other vertex, skipping only assigned edge conflicts and partial triples containing both a duplicated color and a different color. No valid completion can be pruned, and every remaining complete word is directly checked against properness and the positive-odd-multiplicity condition. The complete run made 130,976 calls and found 84 root-fixed assignments, all of sizes (4,8,8,8). There are four equal-sized choices for the root color; forgetting names gives six root-fixed assignments per partition because all four classes are used. Computing graph distances and checking all 20,475 four-subsets gives the 14 displayed D_i^± sets by the six exact-distance-four tests. The search checks that these are exactly the size-four classes, with each extending to exactly one partition. Index translation preserves both signs, and index reflection exchanges them, preserving the cyclic graph edges. Uniqueness then transfers this transitive action on size-four sets to the partitions.
residual_risks: The search is a complete finite computation for this specific graph only; the frozen submitted scripts were inspected, not executed. The independent replay uses its default full depth, not the optional truncated mode. It checks the cyclic graph; the separate frozen edge-bijection certificate connects that model to the standard Fano graph.

value.rationale: The Coxeter graph is a canonical symmetric cubic graph, and the natural question here is the structure of all optimal strong odd colorings, not a single arbitrary test-instance value. The exact answer ties neighborhood parity to the graph metric: four mutually maximally distant vertices determine the whole remaining partition, and all optima lie in one orbit. This concrete correspondence gives a useful classification beyond an otherwise routine finite coloring count.
residual_risks: The result is not a classification of all cubic graphs and does not assert a general color-distance rigidity theorem.
